why: One function decides what looks like a credential, in Go (cli/internal/model/redact.go) and Python (shared/culprit_model/redaction.py). Both are held to these cases: the exact text each must give back, and whether looks_like_credential is true.

Phase 37 part 1 widens it before any statement text is read (PERFORMANCE_PLAN.md, Phase 37, carried in from the Phase 35 close-out, F2): password=… outside a URL, Slack tokens, and user:pass@host with no scheme. A connection string or a password literal in a normalised statement is exactly what it must catch.

Phase 44 batch 1 (FIELD_READINESS_PLAN.md §6, decision 2; F44-002): this fixture is the promise. Free text from outside Culprit is redacted by this pattern, and its coverage is exactly these rows: 'cases' (each credential redacted, the key kept where there is one, so a subject or probe id never disappears with its value), 'survive' (text that must come back unchanged and is not credential-shaped: subjects, digests, URLs without credentials, Culprit's own reasons) and 'over_redacted' (ordinary text the pattern removes, accepted, each with why). A shape not here is not promised (docs/SECURITY.md §8).
